parsed.rationale: Both `PlayerRateDidChangeMessage` and `HLSRateDidChangeMessage` are `type-alias-object` declarations with empty `fields_or_signature` lists, meaning they are structurally identical only because they are both empty type aliases — not because they encode the same domain concept. `PlayerRateDidChangeMessage` lives in `RadioPlayer/Messages/RadioPlayerMessages.swift` and represents a rate-change event in the generic radio player layer, while `HLSRateDidChangeMessage` lives in `HLSPlayer/Messages/HLSPlayerMessages.swift` and represents the same event specifically within the HLS player subsystem. These are intentionally distinct message types serving different abstraction layers within the `Playback` package; collapsing them would conflate two separate messaging domains. The structural overlap is purely coincidental and a consequence of both being empty type aliases.
